meta.scenario: BPM bridge via breakdown — 8 BPM gap masked by kick-free breakdown window; tempo shift imperceptible without a reference kick

transition_arc: 8 BPM gap (124→132) exceeds the ±4 BPM safe threshold for a standard blend. The mechanism that makes large BPM gaps audible is kick-to-kick comparison: when two kicks play simultaneously at different tempos, the listener hears flam (two offbeat strikes). During T1's 16-bar breakdown (bars 64–80), the kick is absent. Without a reference kick, the brain's tempo-tracking anchor is gone — the ear tracks only hi-hats and atmospheric elements, which are rhythmically looser and cannot register a tempo discrepancy. T2's kick enters at bar 80 at 132 BPM, already synced. The listener experiences: T1's groove → kick-free breakdown → T2's new groove at a faster pace. The tempo change is attributed to 'the new track' rather than 'the DJ changed BPM,' which is the desired read. Camelot 6A→7A (+1) is fully compatible.

annotated_actions.why: Bass pre-cut 8 bars before T2 enters. T1's breakdown begins at bar 64 and strips out the kick naturally — the eq(low=0.0) acts as explicit confirmation that sub-bass is removed before T2's 132 BPM intro arrives.
Kill T2 bass at fade start — prevents dual basslines during blend. EQ is persistent; will be restored at bass_swap point.

annotated_actions.t1_state: T1 bar 64: breakdown starts — kick ABSENT, only hi-hats + filtered pads, drums=0.12, harmonic=0.20, rms=0.16
annotated_actions.t2_state: T2 bar 0 at 132 BPM: sparse intro, hi-hats + atmospheric pads, kick low volume
annotated_actions.why: T2 enters on bar 1 of T1's kick-free breakdown. drums:0.25 — T2's kick introduced at low volume. This is the BPM bridge mechanism: T2's kick is audible but quiet while T1's kick is absent. The brain cannot compare two kicks (one is absent), so the 8 BPM difference cannot register as flam. By bars 72–80 as T2's kick gain rises through the fade, the brain has already partially reset its tempo expectation. other:0.5 — T2's atmospheric pads blend with T1's breakdown pads; Camelot +1 means harmonic compatibility is fine. from_bar=0 because T2's 132 BPM intro starts from bar 0. stems={drums:0.8, bass:0.0, other:0.6} — T2 enters with 80% drums, no bass (held for bass_swap), 60% atmosphere.

annotated_actions.why: Midpoint of 16-bar fade window (64 + 8 = 72). T1 kick absent since bar 64. T1 bass killed since bar 56. The swap at bar 72 is largely administrative — it formally releases T2's bass stem into the mix. T1 has almost no low-end contribution at this point.
Restore T2 bass at bass_swap point — T1 bass is now HPF-cut, T2 bass can come in.

annotated_actions.why: Simultaneous with T2 fade_in. T1's sparse breakdown audio fades to zero by bar 80. The audience hears T1's atmospheric elements dissolving while T2's 132 BPM framework rises underneath. No kick collision occurs because T1's kick never returns.

annotated_actions.why: T2 full groove at 132 BPM fires as T1 reaches zero. The audience experiences: T1 breakdown (kick-absent, 16 bars) → T2 new groove at faster pace. The tempo jump is never perceived as a DJ mistake because there was no reference kick during the 16-bar window. from_bar = fade_in.from_bar(0) + fade_in.duration_bars(16) = 16.
